evidence.quote: that he was darting a contemptuous look on the stately monument. One sees what one brings
Without malice, one might find it more instructive than a whole lecture of Ruskin.

adjudications.reason: In the revision Ruskin is named only in 'Ruskin brought reaction against the Revolution.' Nothing introduces him, so 'One sees what one brings' has no second observer to set against Gibbon. The plan's continuity check requires the Ruskin contrast. The Gibbon-respect clause is not repaired: 'trying to persuade his readers--perhaps himself' still carries the irony.

evidence.quote: St. Gaudens had passed beyond all.
To Adams she became more than ever a channel of force; to St. Gaudens she remained as before a channel of taste.

adjudications.reason: This is a legitimate compression. The episode still sets Gibbon, Ruskin and St. Gaudens side by side ('St. Gaudens had passed beyond all'). It also resolves in V7, so Adams's interest in the artist's response is still evident.

evidence.quote: yet his mind was ready to feel the force of all, though the rays were unborn and the women were dead.

adjudications.reason: The objection would sharpen the anecdote. Even so, the chemist still serves as proof of the method: before radium existed, his mind 'was ready to feel the force of all'. The word budget does not allow a restoration of about 30 words without deeper cuts elsewhere.

evidence.quote: incapable of expression in horse-power. What mathematical equivalent could he suggest as the value of a Branly coherer?
Clearly if the historian was bound to reduce all these forces to a common value

adjudications.reason: The lack of a common scale is still established. The text calls the new forces 'incapable of expression in horse-power' and asks for the 'mathematical equivalent' of a Branly coherer. Paragraph 8 picks up that premise with 'reduce all these forces to a common value'.

evidence.quote: Any one brought up among Puritans knew that sex was sin. In any previous age, sex was strength.

adjudications.reason: The closing line still works as an ironic pivot from sexless art back to measurement. 'Sex was sin' against 'sex was strength' already frames the moral/force distinction.

evidence.quote: Adams had never realized that any other could be in sound taste. Artists felt a railway train as power
Only since 1895 had he begun to feel the Virgin or Venus as force, and not everywhere even so.

adjudications.reason: Without the 1895 qualification, the forty years of American taste is left without its turn. Adams never admits that his own sense of the Virgin as force is recent and partial. The sentence is short and comes verbatim from the first draft.

evidence.quote: they had never supposed themselves required to know what they were talking about. Adams had even published

adjudications.reason: 'Even' still has an antecedent in the historians who never supposed themselves required to know what they meant. The failure ('satisfied him as little as at Harvard') and the progression of sequences towards force survive intact.

remaining_concerns: F3: the chemist's amused objection would make the Boston chemist anecdote better motivated if words become available.
The clause on Gibbon's actual respect for the monument stays cut; the irony now rests only on 'perhaps himself'.
